passage: Ten minutes to the relay. Damini was tying her spikes at the edge of the Aizawl track when Lalremsiami strolled over, ribbon still around her neck. "Beat you in the 200 by a whole second. Maybe next time try running?" A few girls giggled. Damini's face went hot and she wanted to fire something back. But the relay was coming and she needed her legs, not a fight. She looked up. "Congratulations. You ran well." Then she turned and walked to her lane. It stung the whole way. She fixed her eyes on the baton in her hand and thought, one second, I can find one second. She ran her leg clean and quick, and she took the sting home with her as a plan.

qa.q: How long before the relay did Lalremsiami come over to Damini?
What did Damini want to do at first, and why did she not do it?
qa.a: She wanted to fire something back, but the relay was coming and she needed her energy for it, not a fight.

qa.q: What did Damini do that showed a wise way to handle a boasting rival?
qa.a: She stayed composed, congratulated her briefly and used the sting as fuel by focusing on finding one second, instead of trading insults or hiding away.

qa.q: How might Lalremsiami have felt when Damini congratulated her?
qa.a: Possibly disappointed not to get a reaction, or perhaps a little embarrassed at how her boast landed. Damini's calm reply gave her nothing to argue with.

grounding: A rival boasts about beating the protagonist, who stays composed, congratulates briefly and uses the sting as fuel.

passage:
Maria saw the photo before she even reached the colony gate: Nirmala holding the inter-school quiz trophy, and under it, in the society chat, "Told you I'd crush her 😎."

By evening Nirmala was at the park swings, telling a group of Class 9 kids how Maria had "frozen" on the final buzzer round. Maria heard her own name as she walked past with the milk packets.

Her face burned. She could turn and say something about the question Nirmala had guessed. She could skip the park for a week.

Instead she stopped, put the bag down, and said, "Congrats, Nirmala. You were quicker on the buzzer." Then she picked up the milk and went home.

Upstairs she opened her notebook and wrote "buzzer practice, fifteen minutes a day" across the top of a fresh page. The sting was still there. She planned to use it.

qa.q: What was Maria carrying when she walked past the park?
qa.a: Maria was carrying the milk packets.

qa.q: What was Maria feeling when she heard her name at the swings?
qa.a: Maria felt humiliated and angry, with her face burning, and was tempted to snap back or hide for a week.

qa.q: What did Maria do that was wise, and why?
qa.a: She congratulated Nirmala briefly and calmly, then turned the sting into buzzer practice, which kept her dignity and gave her a way to improve.

qa.q: How might Nirmala see Maria's short congratulations?
qa.a: Nirmala might be caught off guard, since she expected Maria to be upset, and the calm reply may take some fun out of the boasting.

grounding: It shows a teen whose rival boasts about beating her, who stays composed, congratulates briefly and uses the sting as fuel instead of insulting back or hiding.

passage:
"So, class rep, huh?" Arnab dropped his bag on the desk next to Swati's. "Twenty-two votes to your nine. Guess people know who can actually lead."

Swati kept her eyes on her notebook for a second. "Congratulations, Arnab. You ran a good campaign."

"That's it? No speech? I thought you'd at least say it was rigged."

"It wasn't rigged."

"You're just saying that."

"No." She closed the notebook. "I lost. It stings. I'm not going to pretend it doesn't, and I'm not going to fight you about it either."

Arnab shrugged, a bit thrown. "Okay… so what, you're done with the whole student council thing?"

"Not even close. The eco-club election is next month. I'm going to ask around what people wanted from a rep and didn't hear from me."

"You're weird, Swati."

"Maybe. See you at assembly."

qa.q: How many votes did Swati get?
What was Swati feeling when Arnab listed the votes?
qa.a: Swati felt disappointed and stung, keeping her eyes down for a moment and admitting that losing stings, even while she stayed calm.

qa.q: What could Swati do next to use the loss well?
qa.a: Swati could follow through on asking classmates what they wanted from a rep, so the eco-club campaign answers their needs.

qa.q: How does Arnab see Swati's calm reaction?
qa.a: Arnab seems thrown and a little puzzled, since he expected her to be angry or blame the vote, and ends up calling her weird.

grounding: It shows a rival gloating over a win and the teen who stays composed, congratulates briefly and uses the sting as fuel.
